edits.old: Node.js cursors support cursorLifetime and iteration timeout modes. Non-tailable cursors default to cursorLifetime; tailable cursors default to iteration, which budgets each next() call. (high confidence)
edits.new: Node.js cursors support cursorLifetime and iteration timeout modes. Non-tailable cursors default to cursorLifetime; tailable cursors default to iteration, which budgets each next() call. (high confidence) Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/node/current/connect/connection-options/csot.md

evidence.quote: To configure the mode, set the `timeoutMode` option to `cursorLifetime`, which is the default, or `iteration`.
The cursor iteration mode uses the `timeoutMS` option to limit each call to the `next()`, `hasNext()`, or `tryNext()` method.
This is the default mode for all tailable cursors, such as the tailable cursors returned by the `find()` method on capped collections or change streams.

statements.statement: Node.js cursors support cursorLifetime and iteration timeout modes.

statements.note: cursorLifetime is the default; iteration is the default only for tailable cursors.

statements.statement: Tailable cursors default to iteration, which budgets each next() call.
statements.note: Iteration mode limits each next()/hasNext()/tryNext() call and is the tailable default.

edits.rationale: The Node.js CSOT guide (not the cited EXPERIMENTAL_FEATURES.md) states that timeoutMode is cursorLifetime (default) or iteration, and that iteration, which limits each next()/hasNext()/tryNext() call, is the default for tailable cursors. The cited source was wrong, but the facts are true.

edits.old: The Node.js guide and experimental-features file both mark CSOT experimental; validate behavior against the deployed driver rather than assuming that an accepted specification means a stable implementation. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23)
edits.new: The Node.js guide marks CSOT experimental; validate behavior against the deployed driver rather than assuming that an accepted specification means a stable implementation. (The driver's EXPERIMENTAL_FEATURES.md does not list CSOT in its feature table.) The experimental-features file marks CSOT experimental.
statements.note: The file's summary table lists three features and CSOT is not among them.

statements.statement: Validate behavior against the deployed driver rather than assuming an accepted specification means a stable implementation.
statements.note: Advice, supported in spirit by the experimental notice.

edits.rationale: The Node.js guide says CSOT is experimental and might change. The EXPERIMENTAL_FEATURES.md file lists only Runtime Adapters, AbortSignal Support and Strict TypeScript Types, so it does not mark CSOT experimental.

edits.old: Node.js documents CSOT as experimental. Its experimental-features policy permits behavior and TypeScript compatibility changes even in patch and minor releases. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23)
edits.new: Node.js documents CSOT as experimental and subject to change in future driver releases. Separately, the driver's experimental-features policy says experimental features may change in any release, including patches and minors, but its feature list does not include CSOT. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/node/current/connect/connection-options/csot.md ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/node-mongodb-native/main/EXPERIMENTAL_FEATURES.md

evidence.quote: The CSOT feature is experimental and might change in future driver releases.
Experimental features may change in any release, including patches and minors, and are not covered by the driver's semver guarantees.
Updates can change runtime behavior or break TypeScript compilation, and may require source changes before you can upgrade.

statements.statement: Its experimental-features policy permits behavior and TypeScript compatibility changes even in patch and minor releases (as applied to CSOT).
statements.note: The policy exists in EXPERIMENTAL_FEATURES.md, but CSOT is not a listed feature, so it is not established to apply to CSOT.

edits.rationale: The guide marks CSOT experimental. The patch/minor and TypeScript-breakage policy is real but belongs to EXPERIMENTAL_FEATURES.md, which does not list CSOT, so applying it to CSOT is not supported.
